title: Use a bundled EPP seed workspace for the first scaffold
decision: Archivist v1 should start with a small bundled EPP seed workspace for development and demos while preserving a workspace manifest shape that can later open a full external EPP workspace.
context: The app needs to be runnable immediately and easy to share, but should not trap tool development inside the original Emergency Prep Project process repo.
rationale: A seed workspace gives the frontend and service concrete content without copying the entire generated browser or process repo. A manifest boundary keeps the future path open for full EPP imports, coworker copies, and non-EPP document collections.
alternatives_considered: Copy the full EPP process repo into this app repo
Only open the original EPP repo by absolute path
Use generic fake content with no EPP seed
consequences: The first app can build and run without depending on the original EPP checkout
Seed content must be clearly marked as proof content, not the full EPP migration
The next service slice should read workspace manifests and documents through the local service
Full coworker EPP distribution remains a later packaging/import task
